blocks.heading: What this section covers
blocks.text: State what a point under, a point on and a point beyond a production possibility curve each show, and read an economy position from figures.

blocks.heading: Three locations, three meanings
blocks.text: A point on the boundary shows resources fully and efficiently employed: output sits at a maximum for that combination. A point under the boundary, inside it, shows resources idle or used in the wrong place: output of one good, or of both, could be higher without a sacrifice. A point beyond the boundary cannot be produced with the current resources and technology; it stays out of reach until the boundary itself shifts outward. Location is a fact, not a verdict: an economy inside its PPC during a seasonal pause is not failing, it is waiting for the harvest.

blocks.heading: A worked reading
blocks.text: A co-operative in Katima Mulilo weaves reed mats and carves fish baskets. With its 12 members it could make up to 60 reed mats or 30 fish baskets a month; 40 reed mats together with 22 fish baskets is one combination on its boundary. In March it made 40 reed mats and 12 fish baskets, with four members away and a loom idle. At the same 40 reed mats, 12 fish baskets sits below the 22 the boundary allows, so March lies inside the boundary: both outputs could have been higher had the same people and loom been at work.

blocks.heading: From idle to employed
blocks.text: When resources are idle, moving toward the boundary costs nothing in the other good: the four members returning raise mats and baskets together, since the co-operative starts inside its PPC. That is why unemployment of any resource shows up as an interior point. Once the boundary is reached, further gains in one good come at a cost in the other, and the interior free lunch ends. The Netherlands pumps land from the sea to move its whole boundary outward, and a point beyond reach today becomes reachable once the boundary has moved.

blocks.heading: Connections
blocks.text: The boundary comes from the previous section; what it costs to slide along it is topic 1.4.3, and what moves the whole boundary is topic 1.4.4.
